handoff: AC1–AC4, 09-F4, 08-F4, S12/D8 traced and green; review#2 F1–F7 fixed; post-claim crash windows traced (no start-over in the normal cases). Minor: F1 re-run after a failed/crashed place() with a stale leftover copy keeps it and leases on the newer sha (needs slice 13's cleanup; carry over); F2 record_only story not pushed by tick; F3 messages/fsync/test id; F4 nit.

findings.title: A re-run after a failed or crashed place() can keep a stale leftover copy and push it over the newer record
findings.detail:
keepLocal = mine && existsSync(storyRunStateDir) does not ask whether the local run state is the remote's record. Scenario: A handed gh-N to B and kept its old run state in the machine dir (removing it is slice 13, D11/B27). B moves the record on. A runs checkout: mine is false, so B's record is staged and the claim acquired, then place() throws (record_place_failed, which tells A to run checkout again) or the process dies before place(). (a) A's next tick finds state and a worktree, so start.record_unplaced does not fire and A's old cursor resumes. (b) The re-run has mine true and the dir present, so keepLocal skips staging, and line 305 sets the local ref to B's sha. The next push_record leases on B's sha and replaces B's record with A's stale one; record_moved is not checked because staged is null (:286). Both need the leftover copy plus a place() failure or crash right after the claim; there is no test.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: In slice 13 (or here), keep local run state only when the local record ref equals the fetched remote sha, or when the run state's last take or push matches it, keeping the 08-F4 holder-refetch case explicit. Otherwise stage and place. Add a test: leftover copy, place() failure, re-run.

findings.title: A record_only story is never pushed by a tick
findings.detail:
B33: 'its record kept and handed over the same way'. A story held only from its record returns before pushRecord and the closed-issue cleanup, so under record.policy remote its take and newly applied receipts reach the ref only through a release (story handoff), which is untested for a story without a branch. What `norn status` shows for such a unit (review step, no worktree) is not asserted either.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Let pushRecord run for record_only stories, or test the handoff of one; assert its status item.

findings.title: Post-claim messages and smaller gaps
findings.detail:
(a) record_moved on a claim this checkout already held keeps the claim but does not say so. After --force, 'given back' means the claim is deleted; the previous holder's claim is not restored. (b) A throw from git.worktreeAdd or equipWorktree (:330, :333) comes out raw, without the 'claim is held' note. (c) record-ref.ts:266 place() does not fsync the parent dir after its renames, as writeAtomic does (S1). (d) The rewrite 'seen' check reads only the current round; under local policy a holder that rebases its own branch would restart on re-checkout. (e) The 08-F4 test checks the Check item id only as a `record-push:` prefix, not `:<lease>`.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Say 'the claim stays yours' in the held case, wrap the worktree errors, fsync the parent dir, and assert the full item id.

findings.title: A stray /** swallows RECORD_PUSH_EFFECT's doc comment
findings.detail:
A lone `/**` at 175–176 opens a doc comment that runs into the next one.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Remove it.
